title: Monument Valley and Rifle: Monitoring Plant-Based Approaches to Milling Site Remediation
summary: The Department of Energy’s Office of Legacy Management (DOE-LM) is using cutting-edge technology to give its scientists a virtual look underground at its Monument Valley processing site in Arizona, where a uranium mill once operated. By tracking the size and movements of a nitrate plume below the site, DOE-LM is assessing the effectiveness of a plant-based treatment plan. Plants are also key to environmental remediation at a former uranium mill site in Rifle, Colo. There, DOE-LM is planting and seeding vegetation with the aim of reducing the amount of groundwater that reaches a buried disposal cell.

title: European new nuclear: Italian revival, Polish agreement, Parisian summit
summary: Recent news from the international nuclear community includes progress across Europe. In Italy, the Senate passed a bill allowing the government to build a framework to bring back nuclear power. Plans for Poland’s first nuclear power plant are moving forward, with a partnership between Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe and a Bechtel-Westinghouse consortium now in place. Partners have crafted a memorandum of understanding for the potential deployment of GE Vernova Hitachi’s BWRX-300 in Europe and the United Kingdom. And earlier this month, the Roadmaps to New Nuclear conference was held in Paris, France, where OECD Nuclear Energy Agency Director General William Magwood IV gave the opening address.

title: Incident pauses Palisades fuel loading; plant connected to switchyard
summary: An incident involving a fuel assembly has paused the fuel loading process at the Palisades power plant in Covert, Mich., operator Holtec has acknowledged. Fuel loading began on August 30 as Palisades entered Mode 6, the refueling stage of the restart. The reactor core consists of 204 fuel assemblies that include new fuel and partially used fuel from the plant’s most recent operating cycles.
